

<details>
<summary>Let me check the existing file first.</summary>

```bash
cat src/greet.py
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Now I'll add the farewell function.</summary>

```bash
cat >> src/greet.py << 'EOF'

def farewell(name):
    return f"bye {name}"
EOF
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Write the outcome file.</summary>

```bash
mkdir -p out && cat > out/result.json << 'EOF'
{"schema_version": 1, "outcome": "executed", "summary": "added farewell(name) function to src/greet.py that returns f\"bye {name}\""}
EOF
```
</details>

Done! I added a `farewell(name)` function to `src/greet.py` that returns `f"bye {name}"`, following the same pattern as the existing `greet` function.

- `src/greet.py` — now contains both `greet(name)` and `farewell(name)`
- `out/result.json` — written with the outcome
